details.description: Llama 3.1 405B Instruct is Meta's largest Llama 3.1 model, an auto-regressive transformer with grouped-query attention, instruction-tuned via supervised fine-tuning and RLHF for assistant-style chat, and released July 23, 2024. It was trained on roughly 15 trillion tokens of publicly available data (knowledge cutoff December 2023) and supports a 128K-token context window, multilingual generation across eight languages, and tool use for agentic and RAG workloads. Meta describes it as its first openly available frontier-level model. Amazon Bedrock now lists this snapshot's lifecycle as Legacy, with an end-of-life date of July 7, 2026.
advantages: Scores 89.0% pass@1 on HumanEval and 96.8% on GSM-8K (chain-of-thought), per Meta's own reported benchmarks (Hugging Face model card).
Scores 92.0% on the API-Bank tool-use benchmark and 88.5% on BFCL, per Meta's own reported benchmarks (Hugging Face model card).
Scores 91.6% on the multilingual MGSM benchmark (chain-of-thought), per Meta's own reported benchmarks (Hugging Face model card).
Meta reports the model enables synthetic data generation and model distillation workflows at scale (Meta Llama 3.1 launch post).
disadvantages: Amazon Bedrock lists this model's lifecycle status as Legacy, with an end-of-life date of July 7, 2026 (Amazon Bedrock model card).
Knowledge cutoff of December 2023 (Hugging Face model card).
Its 405B parameter size requires quantization (16-bit to 8-bit) for practical single-node inference, per Meta's own description (Meta Llama 3.1 launch post).
use_cases: Long-form text summarization over the 128K-token context window
Multilingual conversational agents across eight languages
Synthetic data generation and model distillation for smaller models

notes: Catalog's deprecation_date is empty for this snapshot, but Amazon Bedrock's own model card marks its lifecycle 'Legacy' with a 'Model EOL date' of July 7, 2026 (the page's separate 'EOL no sooner than' field is a different, earlier date, Jul 23, 2025) -- flagging this conflict since it directly affects the model's current status. Catalog's context window (128000) and max output tokens (4096) match Bedrock's model card (128K / 4K). No Hugging Face 'newer version' banner was shown on this specific 405B card, unlike the 70B Instruct card.
